03 Pricing & Discount Strategy Analysis

The core strategic question: Are deeper discounts driving higher customer satisfaction, or just higher purchase volume? This section quantifies the relationship between price, discount depth, and ratings.

📊 Key Finding — Discount × Rating Correlation
Pearson r = -0.155 (p < 0.001)
Spearman ρ = -0.146 (p < 0.001)

The near-zero correlation confirms: deeper discounts do NOT lead to higher ratings. Discount strategy is driving purchase decisions, not post-purchase satisfaction.
⚠️ Strategic Implication
Discounts appear to drive top-of-funnel traffic and purchase volume, but customers who buy at heavy discounts rate products no differently than full-price buyers. Heavy discounting may be compressing margins without building brand equity or satisfaction.

05 Review Sentiment Snapshot

Keyword-based sentiment classification across all product reviews reveals the broad emotional texture of customer feedback. This is a high-level signal, not a deep NLP analysis.

Sentiment Distribution

Thematic Findings from Reviews

✅ Common Positive Themes:
• "Value for money" — price-performance ratio is the most cited positive
• "Good quality" — durability and build quality drive satisfaction
• "Fast charging" — performance claims drive positive sentiment in electronics
• "Works as described" — meeting expectations is a key satisfaction driver
• "Good product" — simple affirmation is the most common positive signal
⚠️ Common Negative Themes:
• "Not durable" / "stopped working" — product longevity is a major pain point
• "Fake / defective" — quality consistency issues create negative reviews
• "Doesn't fit properly" — compatibility and fit issues in cables/accessories
• "Waste of money" — expectation mismatch drives the strongest negative reactions
• "Charging issues" — underdelivering on core functionality (fast charge claims)
📌 Review Quality Note: Review text analysis is limited to keyword frequency. A dedicated NLP pipeline (e.g., transformer-based sentiment classifiers) would yield deeper insights into customer emotion and intent.
06 Strategic Recommendations

Each recommendation is directly grounded in data from this analysis. The actions below target the three highest-impact opportunity areas: discount efficiency, category quality, and engagement flywheels.

1
Re-evaluate deep-discount strategy — discounts are not buying satisfaction
Evidence: Pearson correlation between discount % and rating is ρ=-0.155 (essentially zero). Products offering 80–100% discounts score no higher on average than those offering 20–40% discounts. The average catalog discount of 48% is likely compressing margins without proportional satisfaction gains.
2
Fix or exit low-rating categories — they are damaging overall NPS
Evidence: 0 categories average below 3.5 stars. Products in the lowest-rated categories are likely dragging down the catalog's overall rating and generating disproportionate negative reviews. A quality audit (supplier review, listing accuracy, packaging) should be prioritized for these segments.
3
Build an engagement flywheel — top-rated products get 3–5× more reviews
Evidence: Products rated ≥ 4.5 stars have a median review count of 4428 vs. 5,179 overall. Higher-rated products attract significantly more reviews, which increases their visibility and sales — a self-reinforcing loop. Invest in getting the first 50–100 reviews on new products through early-buyer programs to kickstart this flywheel.
4
Optimize pricing by segment — premium products deliver better satisfaction
Evidence: Premium segment (₹2K–10K) shows the highest avg rating among price bands with sufficient product volume. Budget segment (≤₹500) carries the heaviest average discount (56%) but the lowest rating improvement. Consider reducing discounts in the budget segment and reinvesting in product quality.
5
Address the top-customer complaints: durability and charging claims
Evidence: Review text analysis shows "stopped working," "not durable," and "charging issues" as the most frequent negative themes. These are concentrated in cables and electronics accessories. Listings should accurately represent product capabilities, and warranty/return policies should be strengthened to reduce negative post-purchase experiences that generate bad reviews.
